title: VS Code gives coding agents persistent sessions with an open host protocol
friendlyTitle: VS Code agents can keep working when you change windows
summary: Microsoft introduced a dedicated Agent Host process and the open Agent Host Protocol so coding sessions can continue beyond one editor window, stay synchronized across clients and run locally or remotely. The architecture supports different agent harnesses while preserving their own tools and behaviour.
friendlySummary: VS Code now runs agent sessions in a separate host. A coding task can stay active and appear in different VS Code windows or on a remote machine.
whyItMatters: Long-running coding tasks become easier to monitor from another window, browser or machine without restarting the session. Persistence also raises the stakes for access control, so teams should treat the host as durable development infrastructure rather than a temporary chat panel.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This makes long coding jobs easier to follow. Because the session lasts longer, its permissions and remote access should be protected carefully.
